channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [8] Altermagnetism in twisted van der Waals homostructures
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Jian-Tao Wang, Yanping Liu

Authors: Junying Chen, Xing Xie, Shaofei Li, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Directly relevant to altermagnetism interest and broader quantum materials research.

Tags: #altermagnetism #vanderWaals #spintronics

Abstract: Altermagnetic states hold promise for spintronic applications but are yet to be observed in twisted van der Waals materials. Now an orthogonally twisted CrPS4 homostructure is shown to exhibit signatures of altermagnetism.

item.title: [6] Optical control of electrons in a Floquet topological insulator
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Ofer Neufeld, Peter Hommelhoff

Authors: Daniel M. B. Lesko, Tobias Weitz, Simon Wittigschlager, et al.

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Experimental realization of Floquet physics in graphene, relevant to topological interests.

Tags: #floquet #graphene #topological-insulator

Abstract: Driving a solid with light can create a topological insulator, but controlling its electrons has remained elusive. Optical control of electrons in a Floquet topological insulator has now been achieved in light-dressed graphene.

item.title: [7] Real-space imaging of moiré-confined excitons in twisted bilayer MoS2
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Cristiane Morais Smith, Pantelis Bampoulis

Authors: Laurens J. M. Westenberg, Lumen Eek, Jort D. Verbakel, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important experiment on moiré systems relevant to broader 2D materials research.

Tags: #moire #excitons #2D-materials

Abstract: Moiré excitons have been widely observed in twisted two-dimensional semiconductors but have not been directly imaged at room temperature. Now, this is achieved using photocurrent atomic force microscopy.
